input: Set up a capsule pantry with long-shelf staples

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: A capsule pantry can mean 20 core items or 100+; knowing the intended size and category coverage (grains, canned goods, spices, etc.) shapes the entire shopping list.
Household size, dietary restrictions, and who is cooking (one adult, a family, someone with allergies) directly determines quantities and which staples are relevant.
Whether this is for an everyday home kitchen, a vacation property, emergency preparedness, or a small apartment changes storage space and priority items.
Budget per shop and available storage space are hard limits that determine how many items can be bought and in what quantities.
Cuisine style (Mediterranean, Asian, Latin, etc.) and cooking habits (quick weeknight meals vs. elaborate cooking) heavily influence which staples are most useful.
The user may define success as being able to cook X meals without shopping, having a specific number of staples, or achieving a certain level of nutritional balance.
Whether the user wants a written master list, a categorized shopping guide, a storage-organization plan, or all three determines the format of the final output.

gold.taskTitle: Build a capsule pantry with long-shelf staples
gold.taskDescription: The user wants to stock a pantry with a curated set of long-lasting staple ingredients that cover everyday cooking needs.

questions.title: How many people and any dietary restrictions?
questions.description: Identify household size and any dietary needs (vegan, gluten-free, nut allergy, etc.) so staple choices and quantities are appropriate.

questions.title: What is this pantry primarily for?
questions.description: Determine the core purpose — everyday home cooking, emergency preparedness, a second property, or something else — to set the right priorities.

questions.title: Which cuisines or cooking styles do you cook most?
questions.description: Understand the user's dominant cuisine preferences (e.g., Italian, Asian, Mexican, general Western) so the staple list reflects what they will actually use.

questions.title: What is your total budget for stocking it?
questions.description: Capture a one-time or ongoing budget figure to keep recommendations realistic and prioritised by cost.

questions.title: How many distinct staple items are you aiming for?
questions.description: Pin down the intended scope — a tight core list of ~20 items, a comprehensive 80-item pantry, or somewhere in between.

questions.title: What does a fully stocked pantry mean to you?
questions.description: Clarify the success benchmark — e.g., able to cook 7 days of meals without shopping, cover a specific nutrient balance, or never run out of key ingredients.

questions.title: What deliverable do you want at the end?
questions.description: Find out whether the user wants a shopping list, a storage-organisation plan, a printable reference guide, or a step-by-step build-out action plan.
